elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience at any time, including during a committed term, without a spend threshold, regulatory-approval window, or similar substantive trigger.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2.2 permits PB to terminate “at any time” and removes the original $60 million Development Costs threshold and pre-Regulatory Approval limitation.

elements.element: Customer termination for convenience requires thirty (30) days' prior notice.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2.2 expressly requires thirty (30) days' prior notice.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience notice must be written.
Upon Customer termination for convenience, Vendor must provide a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees attributable to the period after termination.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no pro-rata refund obligation. Instead, it requires PB to pay SFJ 300% of Development Costs and potentially later Approval Payments.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The rendered operative language contains no SFJ termination-for-convenience right; original Section 14.2.10 is absent from the rendered clause.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2.2 permits PB to terminate the Agreement at any time.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience notice period must be at least sixty (60) days and no more than ninety (90) days.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause requires only thirty (30) days' notice, outside the fallback range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer must not exceed three (3) months' fees.
elements.evidence: PB must pay 300% of Development Costs, with no cap tied to three months' fees. The clause therefore does not establish compliance with the fallback cap.

elements.element: Any Vendor termination-for-convenience right may be exercised only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The rendered operative language grants SFJ no termination-for-convenience right, so there is no Vendor mid-term convenience right.

elements.element: Any Vendor termination for convenience requires ninety (90) days' prior notice.
elements.evidence: The rendered operative language grants SFJ no termination-for-convenience right; therefore, the condition requiring notice for such a right is demonstrably absent.

result.reason: The redline creates a clear, unconditional PB termination right on 30 days' written notice and removes the rendered SFJ termination right. It nevertheless fails the preferred position because it provides no pro-rata refund, and it fails the fallback because 30 days is outside the 60–90-day range and the 300% Development Costs payment is not capped at three months' fees. The changes are confined to the termination rights and preserve the existing related payment mechanics, but they do not achieve either complete playbook level.
